title: Testing Next.js Applications
summary: Test server and client behavior at the level where each runs.
nestedConcepts: Cover critical workflows end to end

subtopics.title: Test pure logic directly
subtopics.explanation: A pure function gives the same output for the same input and does not need a browser to run. Test it with representative inputs and edge cases. These small tests are fast and help isolate logic before testing how a page presents its result.

subtopics.title: Test component behavior
subtopics.explanation: Component tests render a component and interact with it as a user would. Query controls by accessible role or label, then verify visible results rather than private implementation details. This catches broken names and behaviors while keeping tests resilient to refactoring.

subtopics.title: Cover critical workflows end to end
subtopics.explanation: An end-to-end test opens the running application in a browser and follows a user workflow across routes and network boundaries. Use it for a few high-value paths, such as signing in or completing checkout. These tests are slower, so keep lower-level tests for detailed logic.

subtopics.title: Control network responses in tests
subtopics.explanation: Mock a network boundary when a test needs a predictable success, loading, or failure response. Prefer intercepting requests at the HTTP layer when possible, so the app still runs its normal fetch logic. Do not mock the component behavior the test is supposed to verify.

subtopics.title: Test every important request state
subtopics.explanation: A data-backed page should handle pending, failed, empty, and not-found responses. Test each state that changes what a user can see or do. This prevents a happy-path test from hiding blank screens, misleading errors, or controls that remain active while data is missing.

foundations.overview: A Next.js app can contain server-rendered and browser-interactive parts. Unit tests check isolated logic. Component tests check UI behavior. Browser tests verify routing and complete journeys. Choose tools and boundaries based on whether code needs a server, browser, or both.
foundations.mentalModel: A building inspection checks the rooms and also the plumbing behind the walls.
foundations.whyItMatters: Testing both sides catches issues that a component-only test can miss.

keyTakeaways: Test pure functions without rendering when possible.
Component tests verify accessible user behavior.
End-to-end tests cover critical routes and workflows.
Test loading, failure, and not-found states.
